Sara: Heads-up — customer reported repeated 400s from POST /v1/embeddings with an error mentioning "dimension mismatch" and "invalid input shape". They say it worked yesterday. Using SDK v0.9.1 behind a frontend proxy. Ticket #C-4892.
Sara: Customer pasted the server error: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"message\": \"Embeddings request: expected flat array of strings or vectors, got nested array. model text-embedding-3-large expects vector length 1536 if sending vectors.\",\n    \"type\": \"invalid_request_error\"\n  }\n}
```

Sara: And their payload (redacted):
```
{
  "input": [["This is doc 1"], ["This is doc 2"]]
}
```

Kevin: OK this screams client-side shape issue — they sent nested arrays (array of arrays) instead of a flat array of strings. Embeddings endpoints accept either a single string ("input": "..."), or a flat array of strings ("input": ["a", "b"]) when batching. Nested arrays will be interpreted as vectors or fail schema validation. :eyes:

Maria: Also check whether they're accidentally double-JSON-serializing or converting typed arrays incorrectly. Common repros: 
- calling JSON.stringify twice so the server sees a string containing an array literal, or
- sending a Float32Array directly which serializes unexpectedly if wrapped twice.

Jake: Asked customer for minimal repro and headers (Content-Type, any proxies). Provided this curl that reproduces the bad path: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": [["hello world"],["second doc"]]}'
```

Kevin: Ran that locally — server returns the same 400. Fix is to send a flat list: 
```
{"input": ["hello world", "second doc"]}
```

Maria: If they intend to send precomputed vectors instead of text, the payload must be something like: 
```
{"vectors": [[0.001, -0.12, ..., 0.002], [ ...second vector... ]]}  // each vector length must equal model dim (1536)
```
And Content-Type must be application/json; typed arrays must be converted to plain lists of numbers before JSON.stringify.

Sara: Customer response — they say they switched from an internal transformer that returned tokens as nested arrays and a few clients started passing that directly. They also had a React layer that wrapped single inputs into an extra array when batching was off.

Jake: Suggested quick diagnostics for customer to run in their browser/node: 
```
// bad
const payload = { input: [["foo"], ["bar"]] };
// good
const payload2 = { input: ["foo", "bar"] };
```
Send both and compare. Also asked them to log `typeof payload.input[0]` and `Array.isArray(payload.input[0])` — if true, that's the nested-array bug.

Kevin: Also flagged potential ux bug in our client SDK: we should throw a clearer error when receiving nested arrays instead of the generic 400. Filing internal PR to add validation in client v0.9.x to detect nested arrays and return a helpful message with a link to docs. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket C-4892 escalated to eng-runtime and eng-ml, priority high. /escalate @eng-runtime @eng-ml

Maria: Resolution notes to pass back to customer: 
- For text embeddings: always send a flat array of strings for batches. Single inputs may be a string.
- For vector embeddings: send a top-level `vectors` field (or `input` per spec) where each element is a numeric array of length matching the model (1536 for text-embedding-3-large).
- Ensure typed arrays are converted before JSON.stringify, e.g., `Array.from(myFloat32Array)`.
- If using our SDK, upgrade to the patch we just opened — it will validate input shape and provide a clearer client-side error instead of the server 400.

Sara: Customer applied the flat-array fix and confirmed embeddings now succeed. Closing the loop and marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
